newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW-Euro Disney sees no dividend soon.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Euro Disney sees no dividend soon.

text.p: Euro Disney chairman Philippe Bourguignon said on Tuesday that the theme park operator planned over the next two to three three years to use cashflow to reduce its debt rather than pay out a shareholder dividend.

He also told Reuters in an interview that the company was not in any discussions to restructure its debt, which stood at 15.1 billion francs ($3 billion) at the end of its 1995/96 year on September 30. ($ = 5.080 French Francs)
"We believe that paying down debt is more beneficial to shareholders than a dividend payment which in the short term would impoverish the company," Bourguignon said.
"In the foreseeable future we prefer to use cash to pay down debt than to make dividend payments. I'm thinking of the next two to three years," he said.
Bourguignon said the company was "prudent" in its outlook for the current and future years but not "pessimistic".
He said it faced particular challenges in the 1996/97 year begun on October 1.

"There are a number of factors in 1997 that will not recur in the future," he said. "It's the year in which financial charges rise by the greatest amount. Afterwards the increases will be much easier to absorb," he said.

"It's also the year where cost tensions are the greatest...because we have decided not to raise prices in 1997...and because in such important markets as France and Germany, we're not yet on the verge of a strong economic rebound," he said.
"I always favour prudence and volumes. As long as we can show our ability to attract the public in a massive way, we'll be able to solve the other problems," he said.

"We know from the past that it's very difficult to make projections on consumer behaviour in an uncertain economic climate with as high a jobless rate as exists in France and other European countries," he said.

But he added that the company was struggling to combat the difficult environment through an aggressive marketing campaign for 1997 -- "the year to be here" -- and a constant stream of festivities to celebrate the theme park's fifth anniversary.

"What I've said is that we're no longer a failing company. That said, we remain a heavily indebted company which has normal relations with its financial partners," he said. "There are no discussions on today on any restructuring projects."
